articleTitle: Robust Optical Flow Estimation for Wilted Plant Leaves Motion: Predicting Water-Stressed and Well-Watered Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Optical flow estimation is essential in computer vision for analyzing and interpreting motion in image sequences. For agriculture, optical flow can be a powerful tool in predicting plant health, particularly in identifying water-stressed versus well-watered conditions in wilted plant leaves. While traditional methods for optical flow estimation have made significant progress, challenges such as ill-defined edges and blurred motion boundaries remain, particularly when dealing with complex motion patterns like those found in natural leaf movements. This paper investigates the robustness of non-local total variation methods in optical flow estimation for wilted plant leaves. By leveraging the strengths of non-local total variation-based approaches, we aim to improve motion boundary preservation in wilted leaf motion sequences, offering a way to differentiate between water-stressed and well-watered leaves. We review existing non-local total variation methods, analyze their performance on wilted plant datasets, and present a new approach integrating weighted guided filtering to handle edge preservation. The findings suggest that non-local total variation with weighted guided filter achieves robust optical flow estimations, offering potential for precision agriculture applications, particularly in detecting early signs of drought stress.

articleTitle: Expanding the Relevant Judgment List based on Classified Documents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: An Information retrieval system is a software system that provides access to books, journals, and other documents. The IR system provides this access according to a specific user query to retrieve the intended book, document… etc. The better IR system is the system that produces better results in a standard testing medium that contains collections of documents, queries, and relevant judgment lists. Relevant judgment lists are used to match each document to its relevant query, and the result of the IR system is compared to this judgment list to evaluate its performance. Usually, judgment lists are built by specialists in the domains of the document subject. In this paper, we used a Machine learning algorithm to create a judgment list with the least human involvement, saving much time and effort. The algorithm that is used is K-nearest neighbor, and the method that was used is the inverse of the distance. The requirements for this method are a few human-matched documents forming a small relevant judgment list, which saves effort and time, as we said before. The experiments were done on a test collection: Medline, which was composed of 1033 documents with 30 queries. This experiment serves as a preliminary study conducted on a small test collection, providing a foundation for further refinement and validation on larger collections in future work.

articleTitle: Constructing Multi-granular Knowledge Graph with Structure Similarity and Hierarchical Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: The structure of knowledge graph is basically flat and lack of hierarchies to make knowledge graph too general to deal with concrete reasoning problems. There are few work about hierarchical knowledge graph. In this paper, the entity and relation combined method is proposed to divide the entities into groups based on structure similarity. The hierarchical cluster method is proposed with the entity and relation combined embedding representation to construct a multi-granular knowledge graph. The experimental results show that the hierarchical division relied on combined embedding are significantly better than those based on the existing entity embedding methods in three evaluation indexes. The combined embedding can capture the structure information which is helpful to hierarchical knowledge graph accurately and reasonably.

articleTitle: Development and Application of Computer Vision in High-Intensity Interval Training
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning, an increasing number of researchers are focusing on utilizing computer vision to enhance sports performance. This study proposes a novel framework to improve the safety and effectiveness of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) through real-time action recognition and fatigue monitoring. Our framework consists of a three-step pipeline: First, HIIT videos are fed into a human pose estimation model to extract the skeletal locations of keypoints in each frame. Next, a machinelearning-based classifier is employed to identify the specific action being performed by the participant. Finally, kinematic changes are monitored based on principles of sports biomechanics to determine whether the participant is experiencing fatigue. To ensure stability and reliability, a sliding window method is employed, and optimal hyperparameters are determined through experimentation. A HIIT dataset was developed for training and evaluation. Experimental results shows that the framework achieves satisfactory performance in both action recognition and fatigue monitoring.

articleTitle: A UAV Edge Computing Task Offloading Method Based on Reinforcement Learning and the Underwater Lobster Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: With the rapid development of UAV edge computing, the randomness of task generation and the unpredictability of UAV mobility have made related problems increasingly complex. This not only poses a highly intricate integer optimization problem but also requires swift and effective decision-making based on real-time monitoring. Traditional offline algorithms face numerous challenges in addressing such issues and often struggle to meet the demands of dynamic environments. In response, this paper proposes an innovative heuristic algorithm-the V nderwater Lobster Optimization Algorithm-combined with reinforcement learning techniques to dynamically learn the optimal data transmission path. Through this approach, we can flexibly adjust the optimization algorithm's update strategy, effectively achieving dynamic management goals and improving the system's overall performance and response speed. The proposed algorithm successfully addresses the task offloading problem in UAV edge computing. Experimental results show that the algorithm significantly reduces system response time and improves task completion rates, fully demonstrating its potential and advantages in the field of AV edge computing.

articleTitle: Audio-to-Score Conversion Model Based on Whisper Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: This thesis develops a Transformer model based on Whisper, which extracts melodies and chords from music audio and records them into ABC notation. A comprehensive data processing workflow is customized for ABC notation, including data cleansing, formatting, and conversion, and a mutation mechanism is implemented to increase the diversity and quality of training data. This thesis innovatively introduces the “Orpheus' Score”, a custom notation system that converts music information into tokens, designs a custom vocabulary library, and trains a corresponding custom tokenizer. Experiments show that compared to traditional algorithms, the model has significantly improved accuracy and performance. While providing a convenient audio-to-score tool for music enthusiasts, this work also provides new ideas and tools for research in music information processing.

articleTitle: Frequency-Domain Assisted Fundus Image Enhancement Network Based on the Mamba Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Enhancing fundus images is crucial for early diagnosis and monitoring of retinal diseases. Although CNN and Transformer-based methods have made great progress, CNNs struggle with long-range dependencies, and Transformers face challenges with large model sizes and low computational efficiency. To address these issues, Selective Structured State-Space Models (SSMs) offer an efficient solution with linear complexity. However, standard Mamba models still suffer from local pixel information loss and channel redundancy, limiting their performance in fundus image enhancement. We propose MambaFE, which incorporates localized refinement and an advanced channel attention mechanism to resolve challenges such as pixel detail loss and excessive channel information. Considering that retinal structures play a vital role in fundus analysis, retaining these structures during the enhancement process is crucial. As retinal structures are predominantly located within the high-frequency components of fundus images, we introduce a frequency-guided approach to capture reliable representations of these features, ensuring improved retention of essential information during enhancement. Comprehensive experimental findings indicate that the proposed MambaFE outperforms contemporary fundus image enhancement techniques, significantly enhancing the quality of clinically low-quality and synthetically degraded fundus images, while offering robust support for real-world medical applications.

articleTitle: Evaluating Tourism Service Quality Using Large Language Models: A Sentiment Analysis Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of the tourism industry, understanding and enhancing tourism service quality has become increasingly critical. This study introduces an innovative method for evaluating tourism service quality using large language models (LLMs) and aspect-based sentiment analysis of travelogue data. By leveraging the advanced capabilities of LLMs, this method enables nuanced sentiment recognition at the aspect level, which significantly enhances the understanding of customer sentiments towards various tourism services. Analyzing over 1,000 travelogues sourced from an online platform, this research reveals the strengths of using LLMs in processing large volumes of unstructured data, resulting in a richer, data-driven understanding of customer experiences. The insights derived from this study provide valuable information for industry stakeholders, empowering them to tailor their services more effectively and ultimately enhance overall tourist satisfaction.

articleTitle: An Inter-Layer Volumetric Attention Network for Teeth Segmentation in Cross-FOV CBCT Dental Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Accurate teeth segmentation is the foundation of intelligent analysis in dental CBCT images and has significant application value for oral clinical practice. The existing teeth segmentation algorithms mainly focus on the oral image with a global field of view. However, in clinical data, CBCT oral data has significant differences in the field of views. This paper proposes a cross-view oral CBCT teeth segmentation network based on an inter-layer volumetric attention network to address the challenges of different perspectives. Firstly, a 3D inter-layer cross-attention mechanism was designed to handle different visual field features effectively. Secondly, a target scale normalization strategy based on physical resolution is introduced to align teeth in various field of views. Finally, a local random cropping training strategy is adopted to improve the robustness of the teeth segmentation network. In addition, this paper also excludes areas unrelated to teeth through ROI detection. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves robust and accurate cross-field segmentation in clinical CBCT oral images.

articleTitle: A Novel Adaptive LSHADE Algorithm for Wind Farm Layout Optimization with Complex Wake Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: As fossil fuel reserves diminish, the urgency for clean, renewable energy has grown, with wind energy emerging as a leading solution. However, optimizing wind farm layouts remains particularly challenging due to the complex wake effect, which significantly reduces energy conversion efficiency. Traditional mathematical approaches struggle to effectively solve the Wind Farm Layout Optimization (WFLO) problem. In response, this study proposes a Novel Adaptive LSHADE Algorithm (A-LSHADE) designed to address WFLO with complex wake effect. The algorithm adaptively guides the search process by selecting the optimal individuals at each iteration. Comprehensive experiments were performed under three different wind scenarios, analyzing the impact of varying turbine quantities on conversion efficiency. The results demonstrate that the proposed LSHADE variant consistently outperforms six state-of-the-art competitors in all tested conditions, delivering superior conversion efficiency.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Nested Closed-Form Dynamics Modeling and Recursive Planning for Modular Distributed Electric Drive Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: To satisfy the heavy transport tasks for oversized items, enhancing the flexibility and maneuverability of modular transport platforms, to prevent interference during unit coordination in the transport process, which could lead to stress damage to cargo or major safety incidents like platform rollover or tipping, this paper proposes a dynamics modeling method applicable to distributed electric drive multi-axle vehicles. In this approach, the mathematical analytical form of the vehicle configuration can be obtained without introducing extra auxiliary variables, increasing the model's generality and applicability, providing an effective approach to the modeling problem of vehicles with expandable configurations. The proposed control method adheres to recursive characteristics, utilizing recursive task decomposition and coordinated control to achieve the breakdown from overall vehicle motion tasks to individual unit tasks, converting the complex control issues of multiple intelligent units into a unit control problem with modular layer-by-layer nesting, supporting the coordinated control of scalable configurations.

articleTitle: Research on Inertial Navigation Simulation Based on AirSim
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Simulating unmanned systems in a virtual environment has become a crucial approach for the development of navigation technologies. This paper presents a drone simulation platform based on AirSim. It analyzes the deficiencies of the system's built-in inertial navigation simulation sensors and designs a method to generate inertial navigation simulation data based on the true state values of the drone, through the inverse process of inertial navigation calculations. Finally, the algorithm is tested through simulation flight experiments, confirming the feasibility of the approach proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Pre-Welding Defect Detection in Hull Construction Based on Dual-Branch Attention Feature Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: In hull construction, manually identifying and assessing pre-welding defects is a challenging and time-consuming task, with potential defects posing significant safety risks. Fortunately, with the advancement of deep learning, convolutional neural network (CNN)-based recognition models have been successfully applied to computer vision tasks. However, due to the diversity of interfering factors in pre-welding defect images, current models struggle to capture critical defect features. When using attention mechanisms to address this issue, attention shifts can occur, leading to lower model recognition accuracy. To address the issue of attention shift, this paper proposes a Dual-Branch Attention Enhancement module (DBAE). This module extends traditional attention mechanisms by introducing an additional branch focused on enhancing defect features, guiding the attention towards these critical features, and improving feature extraction. Experimental results demonstrate that the DBAE module has superior feature capture capabilities compared to other classic attention modules, with the most significant improvement reaching 7.25 %, consistently outperforming other attention mechanisms. Furthermore, the results confirm that DBAE is effective across various classic classification networks, exhibiting good generalizability.

articleTitle: Enhancing Semantic Segmentation Through a Targeted Approach to Hard-to-Classify Examples
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: This research paper examines the effectiveness of semantic segmentation utilizing a weighted cross-entropy loss function. A modified version of cross-entropy loss is implemented to address data imbalance and improve predictions for hard-to-classify classes. Hyperparameters of the deep learning model are adjusted based on this modified loss function. The performance of the proposed loss function is evaluated through standard metrics.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Strategy for Wind Turbine Condition Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Floating offshore wind turbines are preferred for their adaptability to deepwater environments and high power generation efficiency. The control of floating offshore wind turbines presents significant challenges. The incidence of component failures is higher and the production of floating offshore wind turbines presents significant challenges. This study presents a model-free fault-tolerant adaptive control system for blade root moment sensors. We develop an individual pitch controller and fault repair system using model-free adaptive control, circumventing the need for mathematical modelling of floating offshore wind turbines. Fault-tolerant control addresses fault detection and isolation by turning dynamic fault compensation into a real-time control challenge for non-linear systems. Evaluate and replicate the suggested control method using fatigue code, aerodynamics, structures and turbulence. Equalise wheel bearing load, minimise floating platform movement and decrease bearing load in offshore wind turbines. The system demonstrates strong fault tolerance, particularly in scenarios where the blade root moment sensor suffers frequent failures, as its output power remains close to the rated power.

articleTitle: Area Mapping via Pseudo-Label Discovery for Weakly Supervised Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Weakly supervised object detection (WSOD) is a task that uses only image-level category labels to train an object detector. The most common weakly supervised object detection framework uses ‘argmax’ as a baseline to filter spatially adjacent pseudo-labels, resulting in poor-quality pseudo-labels. In addition, the pseudo-label screening method based on IoU will lose many potential high-quality labels. To address the above problems, we propose a novel weakly supervised object detection method. We design a pseudo-label benchmark determination method, called area mapping, to determine the pseudo-label benchmark through the feature distribution of image and region proposals and improve the overall quality of pseudo-labels. We further propose a similarity-based pseudo-label discovery strategy utilizing the spatial similarity between pseudo-labels to discover high-quality pseudo-labels. Experiments were conducted on public datasets and new state-of-the-art results were obtained on VOC07 and surpassed the current state-of-the-art methods with a slight advantage on the COCO14 dataset.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Computational Model for Disease Identification in Cocoa Pods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: The early identification of diseases in cocoa pods is an important task to guarantee the production of high-quality cocoa. The use of artificial intelligence techniques such as machine learning, computer vision and deep learning are promising solutions to help identify and classify diseases in cocoa pods. In this paper we introduce the development and evaluation of a deep learning computational model applied to the identification of diseases in cocoa pods, focusing on “monilia” and “black pod” diseases. An exhaustive review of state-of-the-art of computational models was carried out, based on scientific articles related to the identification of plant diseases using computer vision and deep learning techniques. As a result of the search, EfficientDet-Lite4, an efficient and lightweight model for object detection, was selected. A dataset, including images of both healthy and diseased cocoa pods, has been utilized to train the model to detect and pinpoint disease manifestations with considerable accuracy. Significant enhancements in the model training and evaluation demonstrate the capability of recognizing and classifying diseases through image analysis. Furthermore, the functionalities of the model were integrated into an Android native mobile with an user-friendly interface, allowing to younger or inexperienced farmers a fast and accuracy identification of health status of cocoa pods.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Based on Zadeh Operators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Zadeh operators for conjunction, disjunction, and negation are not considered a good semantic basis for any mathematical logic. In this paper, fuzzy models are specified by Zadeh operators along with a recursive definition of the truth values of implication formulas (as opposed to standard implication truth functions). These models are characterized by a subset of classical first-order logic. This subset is specified as a sequent calculus whose negation rule is different from classical negation inference rules. The recursive implication truth function and the logical characterization justify the use of Zadeh operators in fuzzy systems.

articleTitle: Dynamic Windowing Strategies for Concept Drift Type Classification in Data Streams
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Detecting and classifying concept drift in data streams is essential for maintaining the accuracy and reliability of machine learning models deployed in dynamic environments. Traditional drift detection methods often apply a single windowing strategy across all drift types, limiting their ability to distinguish between sudden, gradual, incremental drifts. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that leverages tailored windowing strategies to enhance the performance of concept drift classifiers. Specifically, we apply sliding windows for gradual drift, tumbling windows for sudden drift, expanding windows for incremental drift, aligning each strategy with the characteristics of the respective drift type. By generating synthetic data streams using these customized windowing strategies, we train a drift classifier capable of both detecting and accurately classifying different types of drift in real-time data streams. Experimental results show that our approach significantly improves drift detection accuracy and classification performance compared to conventional windowing methods. These findings highlight the potential of tailored pre-training strategies in adaptive systems and offer a pathway for developing more robust and context-aware drift detection solutions.

articleTitle: Incremental Learning for Object Detection Based on Self-Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Incremental learning, as an approach well-suited for handling applications characterized by evolving data streams, aligns effectively with the objectives of object detection. However, existing methods exhibit suboptimal performance in addressing issues related to catastrophic forgetting and few-shot learning of new classes. Through the enhancement of existing models, we propose a novel method that integrates self-supervised learning. By employing a feature-prediction collaborative mechanism and gradient stopping techniques, the method significantly enhances the model's generalization capability for new category features while also mitigating the forgetting of old category knowledge during the incremental learning process to some extent. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains detection performance for old categories throughout multiple incremental learning phases while simultaneously improving the learning capacity for new categories.

articleTitle: Table Structure Detection Based on PPLCNet Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: This paper presents table structure recognition models based on PPLCNet, MobileNetV3, and ResNet, evaluated on the PubTabNet dataset. By incorporating residual structures and the CBAM attention mechanism into PPLCNet, we achieve an accuracy of 73.53% and a TEDS of 94.57%. Ablation and comparative experiments validate the effectiveness of these enhancements.

articleTitle: Transforming Speech Translation: An End-to-End Transformer-LAS-CTC System for Chinese Dialects to Minor Languages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Speech translation involves converting spoken language from one language to text in another. However, traditional speech translation systems use a cascaded structure that has several shortcomings and defects. As global trade and economic development continue to grow, there is an increasing demand for speech translation tasks from Chinese dialects to minor languages. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes an end-to-end transformer- Las-ctcspeech translation system for converting Chinese dialects to minor language text. Traditional systems have limitations, and with globalization, there is an increasing demand for speech translation. The proposed system combines the attention mechanism with a joint LAS-CTC decoder and outperforms traditional models in convergence speed and results. It has the potential to become a useful tool for bridging language barriers and facilitating communication.

articleTitle: Enhancing Stock Market Predictions with Granger and Reinforcement Learning: An Adaptive Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Traditional graph neural networks (GNNs) construct static graph structures, which are unable to dynamically adapt to market changes. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an integrated prediction model combining GNNs and reinforcement learning (RL), enabling dynamic adjustment of graph structures to enhance the model's adaptability and predictive ability in volatile markets. Firstly, we use GNNs to extract complex inter-stock relationships from historical stock data, constructing a dynamic market structure. Secondly, through RL strategies within the RL model, we continuously adjust trading decisions to maximize long-term returns and adapt to market changes. This combined model not only captures market trading information but also responds promptly to market dynamics, achieving more accurate predictions. Experimental results on multiple datasets of Taiwan 50 constituent stocks demonstrate that our proposed GNN-RL model outperforms traditional methods in terms of accuracy and other metrics, proving its potential and superiority in practical applications.

articleTitle: Effects of Weighting Schemes on Retrieval Precision
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Finding relevant information in a vast and growing amount of data has become significant since the arrival of the internet. An Information Retrieval System is described as searching and retrieving a list of documents, such as web pages or other items, in response to a user query. There are many weighting schemes, such as Boolean, Term Frequency or TF, and Term-Frequency-Inverse-Document-Frequency or TFIDF. In Boolean, a ‘1’ indicates the presence of a term in the document, whereas a ‘0’ indicates its absence. In TF, the term is represented by the number of occurrences in a document. TFIDF is the most popular one. It combines TF with an inverse document frequency IDF; IDF gives less weight to terms that frequently occur in many documents. With reference to the information retrieval system literature, TFIDF gives more accurate results on the computationally expensive expenses. Term Frequency is less expensive than TFIDF, and the least expensive one is the Boolean weighting scheme. In this paper, we investigated the effect of different weighting schemes and found out that, in many cases, Boolean and TF performed the same as TFIDF and, in a few cases, outperformed them. The experiments in this paper were conducted on many datasets of variant sizes and types. The dataset documents were indexed using TFIDF, TF, and Boolean. Then, using the queries that come with the dataset, we computed the precision and recall by comparing the results of different weighting schemes; the queries were also indexed using TFIDF, TF, and Boolean weighting schemes. The objective is to show that the use of the Boolean or TF weighting scheme, which is considered not computationally expensive, instead of TFIDF, which is regarded as very computationally expensive, does not significantly affect the results and, in a few cases, gives better results.

articleTitle: Real-Time Detection of Student Attention in Online Learning: A Scalable Solution for Crisis-Driven Remote Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has sharply highlighted the issues associated with keeping students engaged in online learning environments. In response, we introduce a real-time system for detecting and analyzing student attention during virtual classes. A real-time monitoring of students engagement should substitute the visual communication among students and educators in Face-to-Face (F2F) learning and subsequently allow the later to adjust their teaching behaviours during the Online classes. By mining the Students Attention Detection Dataset and Leveraging random forest along with feature engineering, Our model captures student behaviours like face orientation, hand gestures, phone usage, etc. in order to differentiate between attentive and inattentive students. Our study, demonstrates that features This research has implications beyond COVID-19, as online learning becomes more of a solution during natural disasters such floods, storms or other crises that impact traditional education. Our method provides a solution scalable to avoid learning disturbance in emergency conditions of remote learning. Early results show that real-time monitoring has significantly increased student engagement and are setting the foundation for more adaptable insights towards teaching during future disruptions.

articleTitle: Tourism Local Knowledge Acquisition via Pre-Trained Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Local knowledge which is rich in travelogue provides differentiation, competitiveness and sustainability for tourism entrepreneurs and tourist, that can be well expressed by knowl-edge graph. Traditional tourism knowledge graph construction method constructed automatically by structured data facing the difficulties in extracting entity and complex relationship in travelogue from UGC data. To address these limitations, an tourism local knowledge information extraction framework for constructing a knowledge graph via pre-trained language model is proposed in this paper. A fine-tuned smaller language model (6B) is employed to extract tourism local knowledge entity, property and relationship from the travelogue generated by user on the online tourism agency platform, enabling automated and universal analysis of textualized data.

articleTitle: Interpretation and Optimization of Shallow Convolutional Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have become a cornerstone technology in deep learning, achieving remarkable success in computer vision in recent years. Despite CNNs' impressive performance in tasks such as image classification and object detection, their internal mechanisms remain opaque, particularly regarding the principles behind feature extraction by convolutional filters, which are often viewed as a “black box.” Shallow convolutional filters in CNNs play a crucial role in feature extraction, effectively capturing fundamental attributes such as color, texture, and edges. This study aims to elucidate the underlying logic of feature extraction by analyzing the weight distributions of shallow convolutional filters, providing a precise classification of these filters. Furthermore, using Bayesian optimization to determine the optimal configuration of different types of filters and eliminating redundant ones, we conducted experiments across diverse datasets and network architectures. The results demonstrate that the optimized networks achieve notable improvements in both accuracy and computational efficiency, with a reduction in computational overhead. These findings offer valuable theoretical insights for guiding CNN design and application.

articleTitle: Pretrained Large Models in Telecommunications: A Survey of Technologies and Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: As telecommunications networks become more complex, optimizing performance and predicting traffic are crucial for enhancing customer experience. Pretrained large models (PLMs) based on Transformer architecture have proven effective in processing large-scale structured and unstructured data, making them a promising solution. This paper reviews key technologies and applications of PLMs in telecommunications networks, focusing on data embeddings, model training, and real-time inference. It also explores applications in network performance optimization and fault prediction.

articleTitle: CA-BPNN-Based Multi-Modal Fusion Teaching Quality Evaluation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: In the context of globalization and rapid information development, enhancing educational quality has become a global focal point. Teaching quality assessment is a crucial tool for measuring educational effectiveness and a key factor in promoting teaching innovation and improving methods. Traditional assessment methods often rely on single data sources, which can lead to subjectivity and partiality. Therefore, developing a model that effectively integrates multimodal data for evaluating teaching quality is essential. This study introduces a multimodal fusion model based on CA-BPNN to address the limitations of traditional methods. The model integrates three modalities: manual scoring, online education platform data, and teaching video data. It employs a cross-attention mechanism to enhance feature extraction and uses a multimodal hybrid fusion strategy to address issues of data missingness. This approach shows significant advantages, with a reduction in mean squared error by 2.4% to 3.9% compared to traditional models. The aim of this study is to provide a more objective and comprehensive method for evaluating teaching quality, thereby aiding in the optimization of teaching management and the overall improvement of educational quality. It offers theoretical and practical guidance for educators and policymakers.

articleTitle: Unite and conquer with bagging-boosting “UC2B” for enhanced anomaly detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: The increasing importance of cybersecurity de-mands effective methods for detecting anomalous behavior in computer systems and networks. This paper presents an approach for anomaly detection that combines Unite and Conquer techniques with Bagging and Boosting methods based on machine learning and statistical models. The proposed approach was evaluated using the UNSW-NB15 dataset, which is a bench-mark for cybersecurity evaluation. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the combination of Unite and Conquer approaches with Bagging and Boosting in detecting anomalies in cybersecurity. This research provides a valuable contribution to anomaly detection, achieving an accuracy of up to 99.5 % on unseen data. This suggests that the proposed approach may have promising potential for practical applications, especially in real-world scenarios where high computing power is not a prerequisite.

articleTitle: Research on Counterfactual Text Augmentation for Text Classification Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Recently, using causal inference mechanisms to address spurious correlation problems in natural language processing (NLP) models has obtained increasing attention from both academia and industry. Researches in this field focus on counterfactual data augmentation, which aims to eliminate the influence of spurious associations resulting from confounders. However, the research still faces challenges, including reliance on manual editing, difficulties in identifying causal text spans, and the need to balance controllability with diversity during text generation. To address the challenge of identifying causal features in text, this paper adopts gradient-based post-hoc interpretation algorithms to develop two modules for the identification of causal features in textual data. This includes the first-order gradient saliency algorithm and the integral gradient algorithm. The experiment demonstrate that the text causal feature identification module, implemented using the integral gradient algorithm, can extract causal spans that closely align with manually annotated causal features and have a significant impact on model predictions. To address the challenge of counterfactual text generation, this paper introduces a class-conditional, sequence-to-sequence T5 model specifically designed for this purpose. The model masks causal features and is fine-tuned using unsupervised unlikelihood training. The experiment demonstrates that the integral gradient based counterfactual text generation model outperforms first order gradient models in terms of controllability and diversity. It achieves a label flip rate of 0.84 (+0.46) and a Distinct-3 score of 0.83 (+0.43). It also improves classification accuracy on out-of-domain test sets by up to 0.877% (MNLI-m), 0.950% (MNLI-mm) and 0.660% (Stress Challenge), approaching the performance achieved through manual editing.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction of a Breast Cancer Assistant Diagnosis and Treatment Knowledge Graph Based on Case-Based Reasoning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: By constructing a knowledge graph in the field of breast cancer and combining the knowledge graph with case-based reasoning methods, a conceptual model of adjuvant diagnosis and treatment of breast cancer is constructed, which provides a theoretical basis and implementation strategy for breast cancer diagnosis and treatment, Q&A and other related fields. Firstly, the data layer was constructed by combining the diagnosis and treatment data of breast diseases in specialized hospitals, related medical websites, and data in the field of breast cancer in the “Breast Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment Guidelines”. Secondly, combined with the ontology of breast cancer and empirical data ontology, the diagnosis and treatment pathway of breast cancer and the idea of evidence-based medicine were integrated to construct a model layer. Thirdly, through the OggDB database, the knowledge graph in the field of breast cancer is constructed, stored, displayed, and applied. Finally, the completed knowledge graph was combined with the case-based reasoning method to construct a conceptual model of adjuvant diagnosis and treatment of breast cancer. The knowledge graph aims to be applied to the conceptual model of assisted diagnosis and treatment of breast cancer based on case reasoning method, and serve the diagnosis and treatment process of breast diseases, so as to improve the efficiency of diagnosis and treatment of breast diseases.

articleTitle: RespiratoryPH: Empowering Low-Resourced Languages Through Multilingual and Multi-Labeled Social Media Dataset Towards Intelligent Public Health Disease Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: The RespiratoryPH, a Gold Standard for a multilingual and multi-labeled social media dataset was developed aimed at enhancing public health surveillance for respiratory diseases in low-resourced languages. Data were collected from four major social media platforms—Facebook, Twitter, Reddit, and TikTok—utilizing a combination of API resources and web scraping tools, resulting in a dataset of 14,081 posts in English, Filipino, and Cebuano. Posts were manually annotated by two groups of medical experts for symptoms related to Acute Upper Respiratory Infection (AURI), Pneumonia, Pulmonary Tuberculosis, and COVID-19. The annotation process achieved a fair inter-rater reliability score (Scott's Pi = 0.3372). Several machine learning models used this dataset for training and testing, which achieved an accuracy of 81% for multilabel classification, demonstrating its potential for intelligent disease surveillance. The study highlights the importance of multilingual datasets in addressing public health challenges in linguistically diverse regions and underscores the need for continued research in lowresourced language processing.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-Based Atrous Convolution for Brain Tumor Detection Using MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Early detection and diagnosis of brain tumors are crucial for improving patient outcomes. While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated promise in detecting tumors from magnetic resonance images (MRI), traditional meth-ods often suffer from overparameterization, resulting in lower accuracy improvements despite higher computational demands. To address this, we propose an efficient approach, Fuzzy Atrous Convolution (FAC), with two additional modules: Top of the funnel and middle of the funnel. In this approach, fewer trainable parameters are required while maintaining high classification accuracy. A novel convolutional operator is introduced in the FAC model that dilates the receptive field while preserving input data, enabling efficient feature map reduction and accurate tumor detection. In the propose model, fuzzy logic improves adaptability and robustness. Experiments on three datasets confirmed the efficiency of proposed approach (FAC) and it achieved accuracies of 98.83%, 99.67%, and 99.56% on Datasets I, II, and III, respectively. Compared with large transfer learning models, Proposed approach has over 300 times fewer parameters, making them efficient for early brain tumor detection.

articleTitle: Literature Analysis and Scientific Mapping of FinTech: Perspectives from Academia and Market
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Financial Technology (Fin Tech) has become a pivotal subject in both academic and industry discourse over the past decade, with over 115,000 scholarly articles in the Web of Science (WoS) database and millions of news articles on platforms like Yahoo Finance. However, the majority of literature has examined only one aspect of these discussions, which hinders the progress and market entry of new Fin Tech innovations, thereby restricting the potential for technological advancement and industry transformation. This paper innovatively proposes a combined literature analysis from both academic and market perspectives. A bibliometric analysis of 3,255 academic articles on Fin Tech from the WoS database, covering the period from 2015 to 2024, was conducted. Additionally, Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques, including keyword extraction and sentiment analysis, were utilized to explore the characteristics of 1,208 news articles on FinTech, sourced from Yahoo Finance from 2020 to 2024. A comprehensive model was developed to explore the characteristics of keywords and their involvement in both academic and market contexts. This approach has uncovered some key themes related to FinTech and provides a comprehensive overview of the connections between academia and the market.

articleTitle: Mask Inpaints Using Downsampled Fast Fourier Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: In recent years, image inpainting has seen significant advancements, with the LaMa model., introduced in 2021, standing out for its improvements in large-area inpainting. Yet, challenges such as inpainting complex geometries, processing high-resolution images swiftly, and achieving realism in filled areas persist. Existing solutions that incorporate diffusion models to enhance realism are hardware-intensive and unsuitable for high-resolution images. We propose a new image inpainting method, Downsampled Fast Fourier Convolution (DFFC), which addresses these challenges. Unlike LaMa's reliance on Fast Fourier Convolution (FFC) for early-stage global context capture without explicit downsampling, DFFC introduces a deep learning-driven downsampling module to reduce computational complexity and improve high-resolution image processing efficiency. This module allows for data volume reduction during processing while preserving global context, comprising: i) deep learning-based image downsampling, ii) an FFC-based inpainting architecture, iii) a high-perceptual-domain loss function, and iv) dynamic large-area mask training. Our method maintains the original model's performance, enhances processing speed, and reduces computational load.

articleTitle: LEECAU-Net: A Latent Entropy-Quantized and Efficient Channel Attention-Aided U-Net Model for Microscopic Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Microscopic medical image segmentation is essential for detailed cellular-level analysis in computational pathology, offering insights into disease mechanisms. However, this task is particularly challenging due to the high similarity between different cellular classes and variability within each class, especially in densely packed or overlapping cell regions. To this end, we present LEECAU-Net (Latent Entropy-quantized and Efficient Channel Attention-aided U-Net), a U-Net-based model designed to improve segmentation accuracy through a dual-attention mechanism. Built on an Inceptionv4 backbone, LEECAU-Net's encoder integrates Latent Entropy-quantized Channel Attention (LECA) and Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) modules. The ECA module enhances the network's ability to focus on essential channel dependencies, while LECA leverages entropy quantification to prioritize channels rich in information, leading to better differentiation between similar structures. We have tested LEECAU-Net on three challenging publicly available datasets: Triple Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC), Multi-organ Nuclei Segmentation (MoNuSeg), and Cervical Nucleus Segmentation (CNS). Across these datasets, our model achieves higher performance metrics than numerous state-of-the-art approaches reported in the literature. The improved results underscore the effectiveness of LEECAU-Net's architecture in handling the complexity of microscopic medical images, making it a valuable tool for advancing automated cellular analysis in biomedical research. The source code and more results are made available at https://github.com/Cmatermedicalimageanalysis/LEECAU-Net.

articleTitle: A Temporal and Spatial Analysis and Prediction of the Impact of the Fukushima Nuclear Accident on Nuclear Radiation in Zhejiang
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: The problem of nuclear radiation caused by nuclear accidents poses a serious challenge to human society and the natural environment, and after the Fukushima nuclear accident in 2011, global monitoring and analysis of nuclear radiation levels have become more important, especially to assess the potential impact of remote nuclear events on other regions. In this study, Zhejiang Province, China, was selected as the study object, focusing on analyzing the spatial and temporal distribution characteristics of the airborne absorbed dose rate in the region and assessing the possible impacts of external nuclear events (e.g., the Fukushima nuclear accident) on the region. To this end, the present study systematically collected air-absorbed dose rate data from different areas of Zhejiang Province, and combined with time-series analysis methods, explored whether the Fukushima nuclear accident had a significant impact on nuclear radiation levels in Zhejiang Province. The results of the analysis show that there is a statistically significant correlation between the air-absorbed dose rate in some areas of Zhejiang Province and the Fukushima nuclear accident after the Fukushima nuclear accident. In addition, two time series prediction models, Transformer and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, were used in this study to predict and analyze the air absorbed dose rate in Zhejiang Province. The experimental results show that the Transformer model is excellent in handling complex time series data and capturing nonlinear relationships, and its prediction accuracy is significantly better than that of the LSTM model. In addition, through the analysis of SHAP values, this study reveals that wind direction is the key internal meteorological factor affecting the air absorbed dose rate, which provides important support for the interpretability of the model.

articleTitle: Prediction of Hard Disk Remaining Useful Life Based on a Cross-Validation Accuracy Weighted Probability Ensemble Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: As one of the most widely used storage devices today, hard drives are efficient and convenient, but their failure can cause significant losses. Therefore, early warning of hard drive failures, facilitating timely backup and transfer of stored content, is crucial to minimizing these losses. In recent years, research on hard drive failure prediction has been emerging continuously. However, many models suffer from short prediction times spans and low accuracy, which can lead to insufficient time for data backup. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Cross- Validation Accuracy Weighted Probability Ensemble model (CAWPE) to extend the failure detection cycle. By in-corporating a softmax function in the model's output layer, the interpretability of the model's output is enhanced. Experimental results show that the improved ensemble learning model significantly outperforms baseline models, including BP neural networks, random forests, and LSTM, on datasets of various hard drive models.

articleTitle: Modified Greedy Delaunay Graph-Based Method for TSP Initialization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Finding an initial solution for a traveling salesman efficiently and with reasonable quality is needed both by the stateof-the-art local search and branch-and-bound optimal algorithms. Classical heuristics require O(n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), and their quality may be insufficient to keep the efficiency of local search algorithms high. In this paper, we present a modified greedy algorithm. It utilizes a Delaunay neighborhood graph to build initial fragments until no more connections are possible. Then it merges small fragments with other fragments. It then connects the fragments by a two-step process. First, the algorithm re-generates the graph and iterates the process until the number of fragments falls below threshold 1,000. After that, it performs a full search to connect the rest of the fragments in a greedy manner. The method achieves gaps of 2% and 17% for Dots and selected TSPLIB datasets, and gaps of 27.4% and 16.6% for Santa and World TSP when comparison is made to highly optimized solutions.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fine-Tuning and Feature Enhancement of SAM for Remote Sensing Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Remote sensing image instance segmentation aims to accurately separate independent objects and automatically identify land attributes. Recent advancements in large models have propelled self-supervised learning, especially with the segment anything model (SAM). Although SAM can generate instance segmentation masks without additional training, its application to remote sensing images still faces challenges, such as a severe reliance on manual prior prompts, inaccuracies in detail segmentation, and insufficient generalization capability. Therefore, to enhance the generalization capability of SAM in the field of remote sensing images, we propose a SAM-based fine-tuning model called AFFE-SAM. This model combines adaptive low-rank (AdaLoRA) and variable adapter (MiMi-Adapter) fine-tuning methods. Additionally, it improves mask quality in the decoder by employing adaptive multi-scale feature enhancement. We conducted experiments on two datasets, obtaining mAP scores of 66.5 for the NWPU VHR-10 dataset and 67.1 for the SSDD dataset. The evaluation results validate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Task Offloading Based on Utility Optimization in Collaborative Edge Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: In collaborative edge computing systems, offloading computation tasks from users to edge nodes can effectively address the issues of insufficient terminal computing capabilities and high latency, high overhead of cloud computing processing. System overhead and utility metrics are critical factors that impact operational efficiency and inform task offloading decisions. This paper proposes a new utility evaluation model and, by considering task completion time constraints and energy consumption overhead, establishes an overhead-utility balanced optimization method to address task offloading problem and enhance system operational efficiency of collaborative systems. We propose a heuristic solution based on simulated annealing and particle swarm optimization to solve the overhead-utility balanced optimization problem effectively. Through experimental simulation testing, our proposed heuristic solution can efficiently achieve the balance between low system overhead and high utility in making task offloading decisions, fully utilize system resources, and enhance operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning with Label Propagation for Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: In practical applications, the acquisition cost of hyperspectral images is high, and acquiring substantial labeled data is difficult, which results in a restricted number of labeled samples using for training. Few-shot learning (FSL) serves as an efficient method to tackle the classification challenges of hyperspectral images (HSI) when labeled samples are scarce. It acquires transferable knowledge from abundant labeled data, that can be transferred to new domains. However, the distributional differences between domains with abundant labeled data and those with limited labeled data make the generalizable knowledge learned from the former less applicable to the classification tasks of the latter. To address this issue, this paper proposes a cross-domain few-shot hyperspectral image classification method based on label propagation. Firstly, the method employs a feature extraction module to capture complex information within samples, then applies a graph structure to the label propagation algorithm. The graph structure effectively captures local relationships between samples and avoids over-reliance on distant samples, thereby reducing the risk of overfitting. Furthermore, it incorporates a Tri-training structure to learn from different perspectives and complement each other, ultimately achieving classification of cross-domain few-shot data. Experimental results on hyperspectral datasets with Chikusei as the source domain, and Pavia University and Salinas as the target domains demonstrate that our method is effective and has good performance.

articleTitle: Quantum-Resistant Secure Data Provenance in Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Internet of Vehicles (IoV) network facilitates an advanced vehicular communication landscape that integrates various infrastructures to enhance vehicle-to-everything (V2X) interactions. However, the advancement of quantum computing presents substantial risks to conventional cryptographic protocols essential for data security, integrity, and confidentiality. This paper introduces an advanced framework incorporating quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms within the IoV's secure data provenance (SDP) protocols. We leverage robust post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) methods, specifically the Falcon-512 lattice-based signature scheme, alongside Verifiable Credentials (VCs) to ensure data integrity, source authentication, and privacy against potential quantum threats. The integration process, security, and performance of our framework are thoroughly analyzed. The analysis demonstrates its resilience against classical and quantum attacks, making it a viable solution to secure IoV communications in the quantum era.

articleTitle: A Multi-Head Collaborative Matrix Joint Extraction Method for the Chinese E-Government Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: In Chinese government texts, the efficient extraction of entities and relationships is crucial for tasks such as information retrieval and intelligent question answering in e-government systems. Most current entity-relationship extraction methods often overlook the importance of entity type information in relation extraction, making it difficult to effectively capture complex multi-type entities and relationships, particularly in the government domain where the semantics are complex and diverse. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-head collaborative matrix joint extraction method, tailored to the characteristics of Chinese government texts. The approach leverages the Mengzi pre-trained model, which is more suited for Chinese entity-relationship extraction tasks, to dynamically encode word vectors from government texts, effectively solving the problem of insufficient information mining. Additionally, a multi-head collaborative matrix labeling scheme is introduced, allowing the model to incorporate entity type information from the text as an influencing factor in relation extraction. This enhances the model's ability to capture entity relationships and addresses issues of complex overlapping relationships and word ambiguity in Chinese texts. Experimental results show that this method significantly outperforms other benchmark models in terms of accuracy, recall, and F1 score on Chinese government datasets, providing more comprehensive and enriched information, and demonstrating strong advantages.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches for Predicting Atrial Fibrillation Risk in Pacemaker Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Progress in Informatics and Computing (PIC)
abstract: Pacemaker wearers represent a vulnerable population, often facing cardiac issues and a heightened risk of cardiovascular diseases, such as Atrial Fibrillation (AF). Timely identification of patients at risk of developing AF is of paramount importance in preventing potentially serious complications, including strokes, limb ischemia, and other cardioembolic consequences. Deep Learning (DL) methods have demonstrated significant efficacy in AF prediction, offering a promising avenue to enhance the management of this condition through electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis. To overcome data scarcity challenges, we have embraced MLOps, a cutting-edge methodology. It offers a systematic framework to manage DL model lifecycles, ensuring robustness and reproducibility from development to deployment and monitoring in our research. However, the scarcity of digitized and labeled data prompted us to explore data generation techniques, including conditional generation and standard augmentation, subsequently subjected to meticulous evaluation. Assessment of diverse data generation methods reveals that ECGs synthesized via conditional DeepFake generation exhibit an improved distribution, characterized by MMD scores = 8.10-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and MMD = 4.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>. This consequently demonstrates acceptable FD, RMSE, and PRD scores relative to a baseline. A series of transfer learning efforts culminated in relatively conclusive outcomes, illustrated by a 98% F1- score and an AUC of 0.97, leveraging a larger dataset. Despite inherent limitations related to data size, this study, fortified by its rigorous methodology, highlights the efficacy of transfer learning, introduces a pertinent comparative approach to data generation techniques, and facilitates the assembly of a dedicated ECG dataset sourced from patients equipped with pacemakers.
